flags.note: The use of שֶׁ + participle to express temporal/causal relationship mimics Greek participle constructions. Native Hebrew would more likely use כַּאֲשֶׁר or בְּפָתְחוֹ.
Another שֶׁ + participle construction that appears to calque Greek participial syntax rather than using natural Hebrew temporal clauses.
The phrase 'as soon as was opened' with passive construction closely mirrors Greek ὅτε ἠνοίχθη syntax. Native Hebrew would prefer active voice with temporal clauses.
Double passive construction 'was given to take... was given sword' reflects Greek passive syntax patterns rather than Hebrew active constructions.
Repetition of the Greek-influenced temporal construction 'as soon as he opened' rather than natural Hebrew וַיְהִי כִּפְתֹּחוֹ or similar.
The construction 'and this one who sits upon it' using שֶׁ relative appears to calque Greek ὁ καθήμενος syntax rather than using natural Hebrew הַיֹּשֵׁב.
Third occurrence of the same Greek-influenced temporal construction, suggesting systematic translation from Greek rather than native composition.
The relative clause structure with שֶׁ + passive participle mirrors Greek τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐσφαγμένων rather than natural Hebrew construct chains.
The indirect discourse construction with שֶׁ + imperfect appears to calque Greek ἵνα + subjunctive rather than using natural Hebrew infinitive constructions.
Another occurrence of שֶׁ + perfect in temporal clause, continuing the pattern of Greek-influenced syntax throughout the chapter.
The analytical genitive construction 'the appearance of this one sitting' using שֶׁל is influenced by Greek syntax. Classical Hebrew would use construct state הַמַּרְאֵה הַיֹּשֵׁב.
